tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: An average force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>125</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> is applied on a machine gun firing bullets each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> at the speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> to keep it in position. The number of bullets fired per second by the machine gun is :

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the net momentum of the gun and bullet system can be written as

F=nmv   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required number of bullets.

125=n×101000×(250)⇒n=50
